searchText: Right, but that analysis in the thread was pre-verkle. Data privacy across contracts can be violated in both trie models with a proper trie proof passed into a call, so extsload would make it much cheaper and more practical. The OO encapsulation construct is still useful, but other contact's storage should not be confused with a secure enclave. My main objection to extsload is still the fragile developer experience. I believe data privacy can only be violated for historic state, not current state? That may not matter for this conversation I guess. Mostly correct, you can prove the state at the beginning of the current block. So there is a narrow window of privacy. You also have to load in a whole bunch of data since i believe your only good hook is the prior block hash. I have written contracts for on-chain proofs. I haven't checked recently, but the gas cost (primarily calldata costs) was around 600,000 for proof of a few adjacent storage slots.
